$comment: The source of sf-change-confirm's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/change-confirm (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-pro@9cbe061); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

heading.summary: What the change is; without one the card is named «What will change».

heading-level.summary: The heading's level where the card is placed.

state.summary: open: the answers are offered. pending: an answer is on its way (set by a press). accepted, declined, expired: only the outcome is shown. Declined by the person here, the surface folds away (hidden) and the focus goes back, with its ring, to the control that put the question, else the nearest focusable place around it or the next control of the page (DEV D2 on C35); a declined state the host sets without that answer stays shown.

expires-at.summary: ISO 8601. Past it an open card reads as expired and says so once with sf-change-confirm-expired.

change-id.summary: The host's name for the change, carried back in every event.

disabled.summary: The answers are shown and cannot be pressed (a send is in flight elsewhere).

accept-text.summary: The accepting answer; empty is Confirm in the page's language.

decline-text.summary: The declining answer; empty is Decline in the page's language.

changes.x-markup: the attribute takes the same list as JSON (markup, the Studio); the property wins; a number in before or after is shown as its text
changes.summary: The values, as JSON in markup; a property set from script wins.

answer.x-summary: The person answered (vocabulary §5 answer). Cancelable: a page that refuses it keeps the question open and the action answers refused.
answer.summary: The person answered (vocabulary answer). Cancel it to keep the question open. The 1.0 names sf-change-confirm-accept and -decline follow it until 2026-12-01.

expired.x-summary: An open card passed expires-at; said once per time (a fact of this component).
expired.summary: An open card passed expires-at; said once per time. The 1.0 name sf-change-confirm-expire follows it until 2026-12-01.

open.x-answer: puts the question again (state open); asked by an assembly (ask, §19.4) it answers when the person answers or the time runs out, with value {accepted, reason, value}
open.summary: Puts the question again; asked by an assembly it answers {accepted, reason, value} when the person answers or the time runs out.

answer.x-summary: Answers as the person would: accepted true confirms, false declines (refused: closed, disabled, prevented)
answer.summary: Answer as the person would: accepted true confirms, false declines. Refused closed, disabled or prevented. answer('accept') and answer('decline') are read until 2026-12-01.

confirm.x-summary: The acceptance (§19.4): data-sf-action="<id>.confirm" on a page button

cancel.x-summary: The refusal (vocabulary §5 cancel resolves to the declining answer): data-sf-action="<id>.cancel"

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16).

accessibility.x-keys: Enter and Space press the focused answer (two native buttons); nothing else is a key of the card

aliases.$comment: Dated aliases of sf-confirm-change for the shim (core/js/aliases.js, standard §16 item 20). The two answers fold into sf-change-confirm-answer: each old name is sent only for its `when`, with the new detail (detail-adds: the old {id} is inside {id, accepted}), and the cancel is shared.

rows.note: {id} becomes {id, accepted}; sent only when accepted is true
{id} becomes {id, accepted}; sent only when accepted is false
a fact takes the past form; {id} is unchanged

rows.section: rename plan R2 (ui-control RENAME-PLAN-2026-11-03), naming decision 2026-11-02
rows.note: the element is sf-confirm-change; sf-change-confirm is a subclass defined beside it until the date
the event name carries the tag
the event name carries the tag

x-summary: A prepared change put to a person: each value as it was and as it will be, two answers of equal weight, until when it can be answered, and then only the outcome. Applies nothing; a press is an event.
x-renamed: events.sf-change-confirm-accept → answer {id, accepted: true} (vocabulary §5 answer); the old name a dated detail-adds alias sent only when accepted is true, one cancel for both
events.sf-change-confirm-decline → answer {id, accepted: false}; folded the same way, sent only when accepted is false
events.sf-change-confirm-expire → expired: a fact takes the past form (vocabulary §5.1); the old name a dated same-detail alias
actions.answer(kind) → answer {accepted}: "accept" and "decline" are still read until 2026-12-01 and each use is noted
css: the six --sf-change-confirm--* hooks become public variables --sf-change-confirm-<name> (single dash, never set by the component, the old hook names stay the internal layer)
x-decisions: version: 1.0.0 → 1.1.0, a minor while the old event names and answer(kind) hold dated aliases (§4.10).
shape: a leaf. It places two sf-buttons and an sf-icon as its own markup; no part is in a role a rule could bind.

events: accept and decline fold into the vocabulary's answer {id, accepted} (vocabulary §5 answer {accepted, digest?}; the digest is the host's, the card never sees one). The old names follow through rows with `when` (accepted true / false) in detail-adds mode: the old detail {id} is inside the new one. answer stays cancelable as accept and decline were: a page that refuses either name keeps the question open (shared cancel).
own-verb-words: expire becomes the fact expired (vocabulary §5.1: a fact takes the past form); its word is lang events.expired.label.

actions (§4.4, §19.4): open, answer {accepted}, confirm and cancel answer outcomes. confirm is the acceptance a page reaches with data-sf-action="<id>.confirm"; cancel the declining answer (vocabulary §5: cancel in a panel resolves to the refusal). open puts the question again; asked by an assembly (ask) it waits and answers {accepted, reason, value}: reason close for a confirmation, cancelled for a refusal, expired when the time ran out, as sf-modal answers (§19.4).

layer (§19.1, §19.4): a confirm surface drawn in place, kind surface, neither locking the page nor trapping focus; it never stands above the page, so it takes no z-index from the stack and handles no Escape and no outside press. It is a layer in the §19.4 sense only: ask opens it and waits for the answer. side-effects: none (no portal, no network).
a11y-name: the heading when there is one, else the runtime word changes-label («Что изменится»); the description slot goes to the description, never into the name (§4.8).
key-effects: Enter and Space press the focused answer (select) -- two native buttons; Tab reaches them. No other key.
item-shape: changes names its fields with `of` (label, before, after); before and after are text or null, drawn as text.
instance ids (§7.1.1, #41): the heading id came from a module counter (sf-change-confirm-heading-<n>); it is the path id and --heading now.
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js, the migration form §5.2 allows.

examples: examples.json has the open question, the pending card, the outcomes and the expired card; probe.json drives Tab, Enter and Space, the cancel, the page triggers and the old names (gate 16, gate 20).

css-variables: the six hooks the sheet already had, as public variables in the Framework's form (single dash, read with the token as fallback, public-variables.v1 rule); --sf-change-confirm--* stay the internal layer, so a page that set them still wins.
side-effects: none. It draws where it is placed.

version 1.1.1: the first paint is retaken on ui-source c020caa: no held copy of the JSON island, no icon-font state, closed surfaces printed closed, no size the code measured; an example may declare a fake host port for gate 24's phase 3.

version 1.2.4: the time a proposal stays open is formatDate and calendarDayOffset of core/js/format.js (core.runtime 1.20.0; reuse audit 2026-11-02, finding 7), in the element's page language as before: the time alone today, the day and month with it on another day. No visible change. Needs core.runtime >= 1.20.0.

version 1.3.0: the tag is sf-confirm-change (naming decision 2026-11-02: sf-[set]-<block>[-<variant>]; rename plan R2); the folder confirm-change, the id smart.confirm-change and the bundle cl-confirm-change follow it. sf-change-confirm stays a dated alias until 2027-01-01: a subclass the Smart base defines beside the new tag, listed in the package rule, in sheets as :is(sf-confirm-change, sf-change-confirm), its events named after the tag followed by their former names (ui-source change journal tag-sf-change-confirm-to-sf-confirm-change, path-smart-change-confirm-to-confirm-change).

version 1.4.0: the element is SIMAI Framework's (owner decision 2026-11-03, component sets, points 11 and 13; duplication audit 2026-11-03 A-5): the question is general, so the chat, view and admin sets compose it rather than one set owning it. Same tag, same settings, events and actions; the Pro package (contracts/packages/pro.package.json, larena.package.json) no longer lists it and the Framework's registry and rule do; the dated tag alias sf-change-confirm moves with it. The behaviour it shares with the plain sf-confirm -- state, expiry, pending, the two answers, the ask of an assembly -- is one module, src/smart/helpers/confirm-surface.js, and its footer one template part. A minor: where the bundle comes from changes for a page (the Framework's smart/ instead of the package's).

version 1.4.1 (2026-11-08): a patch, nothing drawn differently by this element. Its first-paint sheet list names the kbd sheet (component.kbd 1.1.0, docs review R030): sf-button 1.8.0 draws a shortcut's keys with it, and every component that draws an sf-button asks for it before the first paint. Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.4.2 (2026-11-08): a patch, nothing drawn differently by this element. Its first-paint snapshots follow the actions block (docs review R031, R032; decisions C13-C15): the sf-button and sf-button-icon it draws ask for the screen-reader-only utility sheet (sf-button 1.9.0, sf-button-icon 1.7.0), an sf-button-close it draws asks for its own sheet (C14), and sf-input's classes follow its outer sizes (sf-input 1.6.0). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

version 1.5.1: the size rule C18 (2026-11-09): the two answers share the width below the Framework's sm breakpoint, 32rem (512 px), not below a raw 479 px; on a screen 480-511 px wide they now stand as two equal halves, as on any narrower phone. Also: a patch, nothing drawn or done differently. The generated reference gives the action's method its one object argument, answer({accepted}), where it read the parameters one by one (standard §4.4: the parameters arrive as one object). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged. Also: a minor, with sf-confirm 1.1.0 on the shared confirm surface (decisions C16, C22, C25; C19 -- the fix is made once, in src/smart/helpers/confirm-surface.js). The two answers stand on the control ladder's step 1, a field's and a button's, instead of a fixed 1/2; a size a template gives is relative, so a compact region (data-sf-density="compact") brings them to 32 px with the rest of the card. Whenever the question is put -- open(), or the host reopening it after a refused answer -- the declining answer takes the focus (it was the accepting one), so a stray Enter or Space only takes the question back. The accepted outcome is written in the success role (--sf-success) instead of on-success-container, which read near-black on the card in the light theme. Settings, values, events and actions unchanged; there is no dangerous acceptance here, so both answers stay outlined.

version 1.7.0 (owner decision C40, 2026-11-09): the values are drawn by sf-change layout list -- the field the term and «before → after» its description, the old value quiet, the new one in medium weight, «пусто» for an empty one; the «Было» and «Станет» tags and the two fills of 1.6 are gone with that look (C40, R092: no plates). The list stands in a group named changes-label. The three value variables keep working: --sf-change-confirm-before-background-color and -after-background-color paint the values' ground when a page sets them (transparent by default), -after-color the new value's ink (sf-change's after colour by default). Settings, values, events, actions and keys unchanged; the words before-text and after-text are no longer drawn.

version 1.7.1 (2026-11-11, C40 follow-up): a patch, nothing drawn differently by this element. Its first-paint snapshots are retaken: the sf-change list it draws marks a value of up to 20 characters .sf-change__whole (sf-change 1.0.1 keeps it on one line). Settings, values, events and keys unchanged.

$comment: The card draws its two answers as sf-button, the outcome's glyph as sf-icon
and its values as sf-change (1.7.0); a tag it renders is a tag it fetches.
Nothing else: the values are text, and what a change means is the host's.

before.description: The value as it is; empty or null reads as empty.

after.description: The value as it will be.

answers.const: A press moves the card to pending and dispatches sf-change-confirm-answer {id, accepted} (cancelable). A cancelled event returns it to open. The host sets the outcome: accepted, declined, or open again when the answer could not be delivered. The card never applies anything.

description.description: A line under the heading (a code, who proposed it).

forbidden_client_responsibilities: composing a command or a code for the server

untrusted_inputs: heading, labels and values (drawn as text)

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-change-confirm wherever a prepared change waits for a person's yes or no -- an assistant's proposal, a colleague's edit, an import. Promoted from simai/ui-chat renderProposal (owner decision 2026-10-25).
do_not: Do not apply the change in the element; answer the event and set state
Do not leave the card pending: set accepted, declined, or open again
Do not pass markup in values; they are text

accessibility.focus: A section named by its heading (role=heading at heading-level). The values are a description list. The status line is a polite live region, present before it speaks; when a press takes the answers away, focus moves to it instead of falling to the page, and back to the first answer when the host cancels.

changes: standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8: the element is made from component.json; dated aliases in aliases.json
The first-paint snapshot's sheets.json lists the utility sheets its markup uses (retaken on ui-source 5ba9399); no behaviour changed. Nothing to change for a host.
The time a proposal stays open through core's format helpers; needs core.runtime >= 1.20.0. No visible change. Nothing to change for a host on a pair from core.runtime 1.20.0 on.

The tag is sf-confirm-change (rename plan R2, naming decision 2026-11-02: sf-[set]-<block>); the folder confirm-change, the id smart.confirm-change and the bundle cl-confirm-change follow it (were change-confirm, smart.change-confirm, cl-change-confirm). sf-change-confirm stays a dated alias until 2027-01-01: old markup upgrades as this element, the Loader forwards cl-change-confirm, and every event fires under its former name as well, with the same detail. Public CSS variables and classes keep their names. Needs the SIMAI Framework pair whose package reference lists the former tag (core.runtime 1.22.0). Nothing to change for a host until 2027-01-01; new markup writes sf-confirm-change.

The element is SIMAI Framework's: its bundle is in the Framework's smart/ and the Pro package no longer carries it. Same tag, settings, events, actions, words and public variables. A page that loads the Framework pair from this release gets it without the package; nothing to change for a host.

before.description: The value as it is; empty or null reads as empty.

after.description: The value as it will be.
